1.

We have heard Mohd. Saquib Siddiqui, learned counsel appearing for the appellant as well as Mr.
Aaditya Aniruddha Pande, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-State.

2. This appeal, by special leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 09.02.2011 passed by the High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Nagpur Bench, Nagpur dismissing First Appeal No. 127 of 1995 that the appellant had preferred.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Nagpur Bench, Nagpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. The dispute emanates from the appellants grievance that he has been paid inadequate compensation for acquisition of his land for a public purpose.

4. Before the Reference Court, the appellant claimed compensation @ Rs.100/- per square feet and on that basis urged that compensation in a sum of Rs. 22,86,900/- (Rupees Twenty- two lakh eight thousand nine hundred only) be paid besides solatium and interest as per the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short the Act).

The Reference Court, on the application of settled principles flowing from Section 23 of the Act, arrived at the market value of the land at Rs. 77,133/-
(Rupees Seventy-seven thousand one hundred thirty-three only) per hectare with all statutory benefits.

1 5.
The order of the Reference Court was challenged by both the respondent-State as well as the appellant by filing separate appeals.
While the respondent-State had claimed reduction in determination of compensation payable to the appellant, the appellant prayed for enhanced compensation.
Both the appeals were dismissed by a common judgment and order dated 09.02.2011 and, therefore, the determination made by the Reference Court was maintained by the High Court.

6. The learned Judge while deciding the appeals referred to a decision of the Division Bench of the High Court in the case of Moreshwar Shankar Phatak and Anr. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors.,
reported in 2003 (3) Maharashtra Law Journal 127 and applied the principle laid down therein.

entities.text:
Moreshwar Shankar Phatak and Anr. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors.,
reported in 2003 (3) Maharashtra Law Journal 127
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In terms thereof, compensation was determined @ Rs. 10/- per square feet in respect of an acquired land.
This land was adjacent to the appellants land and both such lands were acquired by the selfsame notification.
The High Court, therefore, did not find reason to interfere.

7. Although, Mr. Siddiqui seeks enhanced compensation, we have noticed that no evidence had been produced before the Reference Court as well as the High Court in support of the claim for enhanced compensation @ Rs. 100/- per square feet.
8. We, thus, do not see any valid reason to interfere with the order under challenge.

The appeal is,
accordingly, dismissed.
No costs.
9. Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.
